text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: Elevated 5xxs and websocket disconnects observed for customer AcmeCorp (dedicated-pool-3) via their app gateway. Initial signal: spike in 504s at the load-balancer + multiple streaming client disconnects. Please triage. thread_ts=1848201234

maria (oncall): I'm on it. Reported by synthetic monitors and a pager from routing-alerts. Is this global or only AcmeCorp?

jake (sre): Only AcmeCorp so far. Logs show repeated 504 from our edge LB to the customer's VPC gateway: `upstream read timeout` and connection resets. Error rate started ~02:54 UTC.

anya (eng-runtime): Are we seeing backend overload (GPU pool) or an app-gateway proxy problem? Streaming-specific errors?

jake (sre): Streaming sessions appear to stall after ~60s then reset. For non-streaming requests latency spikes then 504. Backend (dedicated-pool-3) metrics: CPU/GPU usage normal, token pipeline healthy. KV cache size looks okay.

kevin (networking): Customer uses a private app gateway in front of our VPC egress. Their gateway has a few proxies (NGINX) that default to 60s read timeouts. Most likely their proxy is timing out during long streams.

sam (customer-success): Reached out to Acme on the phone. They report client-side retries are aggressive and some customers see partial transcripts. They're worried. I told them we're investigating and will propose mitigations.

maria (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan ideas: 1) short-term tweak: increase gateway proxy timeouts for Acme (if they consent) or enable short keepalive heartbeats for streams; 2) temporarily route their traffic to dedicated-fallback pool in same region that we control (if routing policy allows and complies with VPC constraints); 3) change client retry/backoff guidance. Which are feasible?

anya (eng-runtime): We can enable stream-heartbeat server-side to send keepalive frames every 20s from our runtime. That's a code-safe toggle and should prevent idle closure on intermediate proxies. Can flip this per-tenant via routing metadata.

kevin (networking): Routing change is possible but for AcmeCorp their config pins them to dedicated-pool-3 for compliance. Need account approval to move to fallback; also must consider data controls.

maria (oncall): sam, can you confirm if Acme will permit temporary routing to fallback pool (same region, same data boundary) or is their SLA/VPC contract forbidding that?

sam (customer-success): On the call now with Acme legal/compliance. They said: allowed for troubleshooting but must be short-lived and logged. They gave verbal OK for a 15-minute test.

jake (sre): Good. While we wait for formal confirmation, let's apply stream-heartbeat and increase our edge proxy timeout for Acme routes to 120s as an internal stopgap. Edge proxy change doesn't affect their VPC gateway. Command I'll run in a sec: `rctl update-route acme-route --edge-timeout 120s --per-tenant-flag stream_heartbeat=true`

deploy-bot: Deploy started: update-route(acme-route) by jake. CI checks passed. ETA ~30s.

jake (sre): Patch applied. Monitoring: edge 504s trending down, websocket disconnects decreased. Still seeing some resets between our edge and their gateway.

kevin (networking): If their gateway is the source, we should push the nginx snippet to Acme's gateway operators as a recommended config. Sending snippet now.

kevin (networking): ```nginx
location /v1/stream/ {
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "keep-alive";
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_read_timeout 120s;
  proxy_send_timeout 120s;
}
```

acme-gateway-team: Thanks — applying change to their gateway now, will roll to 2 of 3 proxies first. We'll report back in 5m.

maria (oncall): Also reduce client retry aggressiveness for streaming SDKs for Acme: set exponential backoff, initial 250ms, max 5s, max attempts 4. That avoids overwhelming their gateway during backpressure. Can eng-runtime push a client-side override in the SDK?

anya (eng-runtime): We can publish a tenant-specific runtime hint that the SDK reads and adjusts retry policy for Acme. Will emit a small patch and notify client.

sam (customer-success): Acme confirms proxy patch applied to 2/3 proxies; initial traffic looks healthier. They're still going to complete the remaining proxy after verifying logs. Appreciate the fast response.

jake (sre): Observability check: per-tenant token throughput back to baseline, websocket disconnects ~90% reduced. Remaining errors are tied to one of their proxies we haven't patched.

maria (oncall): Status: partially mitigated. Remaining action items: - finish patching Acme proxies (customer) - enable SDK retry override (eng-runtime) - run 15-minute test moving small % traffic to fallback pool (requires Sam to log) - track customer impact SLA & incident page

sam (customer-success): Formal permission logged in ticket ACME-8732 for 15m fallback test. I will schedule the test now.

kevin (networking): When doing fallback test, use weight 95%->primary, 5%->fallback for 15m. Command: `rctl traffic-split acme-route --primary=dedicated-pool-3:95 --fallback=dedicated-pool-7:5 --duration=15m`

deploy-bot: traffic-split job queued by sam.

jake (sre): Running the 5% test. Monitoring shows no regression on fallback and customer-side logs show fewer retries and timeouts.

maria (oncall): Good. I'll open the incident ticket and assign postmortem: owner = jake (sre), P0 -> P1. Please add timeline and root cause analysis: likely upstream proxy default timeouts + no keepalive on streams + aggressive client retries.

sam (customer-success): I'll send a customer-facing incident summary and mitigation steps (proxy config, client SDK patch, stream-heartbeat).

anya (eng-runtime): I'll cut the SDK override patch and runtime flag by EOD. Also adding an integration test that simulates long streaming with middle proxies.

maria (oncall): Handoff: I'm going off shift at 03:30 UTC. Night oncall is liam. @liam — please monitor the Acme route for 2 hours, check that the remaining proxy patches are successful and the fallback reverts to 100% once tests complete.

liam (oncall): Acknowledged. I'll watch closely.

maria (oncall): Closing note: incident state = mitigated (partial). Customer impact reduced to intermittent only during unpatched proxy window. Postmortem assigned. Will follow up with timeline for RCA.`
